summary: CAA guidance on how GA pilots use the radio in the UK. Know the squawks (7000, 7500, 7600, 7700), read back the key clearances, report the right circuit calls and use 121.5 MHz for emergencies. MAYDAY and PAN PAN follow a set order. For radio failure, set 7600 and keep clear of controlled airspace. Built from CAA Safety Sense Leaflet 22, alongside CAP 413.
sections: Squawk codes
7000 VFR conspicuity
2000 IFR conspicuity (not used in all states)
7500 unlawful interference
7600 radio failure
7700 emergency
0030 lost (UK procedure). Press IDENT only when asked
Select ALT unless told otherwise
Equipment and technique
Voice band is 117.975 to 137.000 MHz at 8.33 kHz spacing
Check squelch is set properly and keep volume ideally no higher than 70%
Initial call: station name then your callsign. Later: callsign only
Answer with the response then your callsign. Avoid fillers like 'this is' and do not use voice inflection to ask questions
Press PTT before speaking and hold until finished
Items to read back
Taxi instructions, level, heading and speed instructions
Airway or en-route clearances and approach clearances
Runway-in-use and clearances to take off, land, enter, backtrack, cross or hold short
Transponder instructions and altimeter settings
Frequency changes, type of ATS service and transition levels
Simple reporting instructions need only wilco
Circuit and aerodrome calls
Standard calls are downwind and final. Overhead join: report overhead and then descending deadside
Final is between 4 NM and the threshold. Long final is 4 to 8 NM. There is no 'short final': state distance instead
At ATC aerodromes call at 15 NM or 5 minutes from the ATZ, whichever is greater
AFIS uses the suffix 'Information' and may issue ground instructions up to a holding point. 'Land at your discretion' is not a clearance
AGCS uses 'Radio' and cannot give clearances or instructions
Unattended aerodromes: use SAFETYCOM 135.480 MHz within 10 NM and up to 1,000 ft above circuit height
Flight information services and transits
Basic Service: pilot avoids traffic. Traffic Service: gives traffic information only. Deconfliction Service: IFR in Class G, with avoidance advice
Request a CAS transit about 10 minutes before the boundary and stay clear until cleared. Read back altitude limits
Pass-your-message order: callsign, type, departure, destination, position, altitude and altimeter setting, VFR or IFR, intentions
MATZ is not controlled airspace for civil aircraft, but contact the unit before entering
MAYDAY and PAN PAN
MAYDAY is serious and imminent danger. PAN PAN is a safety concern without immediate danger
Order: MAYDAY or PAN PAN x3, station, callsign, type, nature, intentions, position (height and heading), pilot qualification, other information (POB, endurance)
Call the unit you are talking to, or London Centre D&D on 121.5. Select 7700
'Mayday out' closes the call. Make a PAN PAN early if things may get worse
Radio failure and lost procedures
Fly the aircraft, stay in VMC and clear of controlled airspace
Check frequency, switches, volume and squelch, PTT, headset, circuit breakers (reset once), an alternate radio, a relay, or 121.5
Set 7600. If only receive failed, make blind transmissions. If only transmit failed, keep listening
Over an aerodrome, observe the signal square, join the circuit and watch for light signals
If lost, seek help early, squawk 0030 with ALT and call London Centre on 121.5. Do not ask for training fixes in a real emergency

cards.q: Who may be unable to give clearances at AGCS?
cards.a: The radio operator, since it is not a formal ATC service.

quiz.q: Which code do you set after radio failure?
What is the UK lost procedure squawk?
quiz.why: 0030 is the UK lost procedure code, with ALT selected.

quiz.q: SAFETYCOM 135.480 MHz is used at unattended aerodromes within:
o: 10 NM and 1,000 ft above circuit height
quiz.why: SAFETYCOM is usable within 10 NM and up to 1,000 ft above circuit height.

quiz.q: An AFIS says 'land at your discretion'. This is:
o: Not a clearance, so make sure the runway is clear
quiz.why: AFIS gives no landing clearance and you decide and check the runway is clear.

quiz.q: Where should you call if you are not in contact with anyone and need emergency help?
There is no 'short final' call. Instead you should:
o: State the distance, such as 'half-mile final'
quiz.why: State the distance from the threshold.
